name: Platinum Planner
subcategory: clinical scheduling and tracking for EMS, nursing and allied health programs
tagline: Clinical and field internship scheduling, hour tracking and skills documentation for health education programs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is not really a personal app, it is a three-sided system: students log hours and patient contacts, preceptors at hospitals and ambulance services sign off, and program directors pull reports that accreditation site visitors will read. A solo build can absolutely replace the student-facing half, a hours-and-skills logbook is a genuinely small piece of software. What it cannot replace is a verified chain of custody on that data, because a self-hosted log that the student controls end to end is worth roughly nothing to CoAEMSP or a state office. The scheduling side also depends on real clinical sites accepting slot requests through the same tool the program already uses, which is an institutional agreement, not a feature. Build the logbook for yourself if you want a nicer view of your own progress, keep entering everything in the real system.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you log shifts, hours, patient contacts and skill attempts against your program's requirement targets, then export CSV and a printable summary.
requirements: Your program's requirement matrix, hours per rotation type and minimum skill or age-group patient contacts, typed in by hand
Somewhere to run it locally, this is a single-user local app
whatYouLose: Preceptor and instructor sign-off, so nothing you record is verifiable by anyone
Accreditation-shaped reports that program directors and site visitors already know how to read
Scheduling against real clinical site capacity, shift slots and site-specific rules
Program-side oversight: cohort dashboards, flagged deficiencies, remediation tracking
Mobile app for logging a call at 3am in the back of a truck
moatNotes: The buyer is the program, not the student, and the program buys because the output survives an accreditation site visit.
whyPeopleStillPay: Programs pay because the record has to be defensible. Hours, patient contacts, age-group distribution and skill attempts are all things an accrediting body or state office can ask about years later, and the answer needs to come from a system with preceptor sign-offs and an audit trail rather than a spreadsheet a student maintained. On top of that, the clinical sites, hospitals, fire departments, ambulance services, are already in the tool with their own logins and capacity rules, and getting dozens of them to adopt something new is a political project, not a technical one. Students never chose this software and cannot leave it.
notes: The student logbook is an afternoon; the signature underneath it is not. The moat is accreditation: preceptor sign-off, an audit trail, and every clinical site in the region already having a login.
prompt:
Build a local single-user clinical hours and skills logbook for a health education student. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/logbook.db, schema created on first run
- Everything server-side in route handlers and server actions, no external APIs

Data model:
- requirement: name, type (hours | contacts | skill), rotation or category, target number, notes
- shift: date, site name, rotation type (ER, ICU, OR, field, peds, OB, psych, other), start time, end time, computed hours, preceptor name (free text), notes
- contact: belongs to a shift, chief complaint, age band (neonate, infant, toddler, child, adolescent, adult, geriatric), sex, interventions (free text tags)
- skill: belongs to a shift, skill name, attempts, successes, supervised (bool), notes

Screens:
1. Dashboard: progress bars per requirement showing logged vs target, hours by rotation type, age band distribution table, list of requirements not yet met
2. Shifts: table with filters by date range and rotation, add and edit form, nested contact and skill entry inside a shift
3. Requirements: editable table so the user types in their own program's matrix, plus a seed button that inserts a generic EMS-style starter set clearly labeled as an example, not authoritative
4. Export: CSV per table, plus a /print page that renders a clean one-page summary suitable for saving as PDF from the browser

Rules:
- Overlapping shift times are flagged with a warning, not blocked
- Hours computed from times, allow overnight shifts crossing midnight
- All dates stored ISO, displayed local
- Seed the DB with three example shifts so the dashboard is not empty on first run

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, preceptor sign-off, multi-user, notifications, scheduling against site capacity, anything claiming to be an accreditation-ready record. Put a banner on the dashboard: "Personal tracking only. Not a verified record."

Deliver a README with setup, npm run dev, and where the DB file lives. No .env needed since there are no secrets; do not add one.
